title: Compact maps factor through a stage up to homotopy
statement: Use universes, quasicategories, coherent diagrams, cocones and mapping spaces from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and compactness and filteredness from [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category]. Let $\gamma$ be an infinite regular cardinal in the smaller universe. Let $\mathcal E$ be a locally small quasicategory admitting small $\gamma$-filtered colimits. Let $F:I\to\mathcal E$ be a coherent diagram indexed by a small $\gamma$-filtered quasicategory, with a colimiting cocone $\iota_i:F(i)\to c$. If $x$ is $\gamma$-compact, every morphism $h:x\to c$ admits an object $i\in I$ and a morphism $v:x\to F(i)$ for which $\iota_i v$ and $h$ lie in the same connected component of $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(x,c)$. In particular, if $c=x$ and $h=1_x$, then $x$ is a retract of $F(i)$ in the homotopy category: there are $v:x\to F(i)$ and $\iota_i:F(i)\to x$ with $\iota_i v$ homotopic to $1_x$. No compactness of the objects $F(i)$ is assumed.

source.place: The identity-factorization argument in the proof of Lemma 5.4.2.4, printed pp. 424-425, applied to an arbitrary given filtered presentation; compactness Definition 5.3.4.5 and the colimit-of-spaces realization of Proposition 3.3.4.5 give the general morphism version. Read online, not archived under literature/. No Stacks tag states this mapping-space version.

proof.text: Write $h_x$ for the covariant corepresented coherent functor constructed in [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces], and put $A=\mathfrak C[\mathcal E]$. Its value at $y$ is the Kan complex $\operatorname{Sing}|A(x,y)|$. Put $G=h_xF$ and $M=h_x(c)$, and let $\lambda:G\to\Delta_I M$ be the image of the given cocone. The compactness clause of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category] applies to this very cocone: $I$ is small and $\gamma$-filtered and the cocone is colimiting. Therefore $\lambda$ is colimiting in $\mathcal S_{\mathcal U\prime}$. All spaces used below are in $\mathcal U\prime$, with their categories and functor categories formed in a further containing universe. The edge $h:x\to c$ gives a vertex of $A(x,c)$ by the rigidification simplex construction, hence a point of $|A(x,c)|$ and a singular vertex $m_h\in M$. For steps 2-4 write $[h]$ for the component of this vertex in $M$. Step 5 will compare these components with the right-pinched mapping spaces in the conclusion; the definition of $h_x$ alone does not assert that comparison. No property of any $F(i)$ has been used.

source.place: Definition 5.3.4.5, printed p.396; setup of Lemma 5.4.2.4, printed p.424. The concrete corepresentable convention is the cited definition.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-space-transport-classification] with its small-space universe equal to $\mathcal U\prime$. It represents $G$ by a left fibration $p:E\to I$, with $E$ $\mathcal U\prime$-small, and represents $\Delta_I M$ by $I\times M\to I$. Its equivalence of transformation spaces identifies the component of $\lambda$ with a vertex of $\operatorname{Fun}_{/I}(E,I\times M)$. Such a vertex is exactly a map $(p,q)$ for a simplicial map $q:E\to M$. Choose one representing that component. For each vertex $i$ of $I$, base-pullback compatibility identifies $E_i$ with $G(i)$ as spaces and identifies $q|_{E_i}$, up to homotopy under these identifications, with $\lambda_i:G(i)\to M$. This uses the stated transformation-space, constant-product and base-pullback clauses, rather than just classification of objects.

source.place: Theorem 2.2.1.2, printed p.74, and Proposition 4.2.4.4, printed p.258; covariant transport and transformation-space comparison, as stated in the cited node.

proof.text: For any $\mathcal U\prime$-small Kan complex $Z$, the dual cocone criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] gives an equivalence $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal S_{\mathcal U\prime}}(M,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(I,\mathcal S_{\mathcal U\prime})}(G,\Delta_I Z)$ by composition with $\lambda$. The transport mapping formula in [lem-coef-space-transport-classification] identifies the target with $\operatorname{Fun}_{/I}(E,I\times Z)=\operatorname{Fun}(E,Z)$. Apply the same formula over the one-point base to identify the source with $\operatorname{Fun}(M,Z)$: a constant functor with value $M$ or $Z$ is represented over that base by $M$ or $Z$ itself. Compatibility with composition in the cited transport statement identifies the induced map on components with precomposition by $q$. Consequently $q^*:\pi_0\operatorname{Fun}(M,Z)\to\pi_0\operatorname{Fun}(E,Z)$ is bijective. Only its injectivity for the discrete two-point Kan complex will be needed.

source.place: Section 4.2.4, mapping-space universal property; Theorem 2.2.1.2. Agent expansion of the component consequence of Proposition 3.3.4.5 and Corollary 3.3.4.6, printed pp.219-221.

proof.text: There must be a vertex $e\in E$ with $[q(e)]=[h]$ in $\pi_0 M$. Otherwise let $D$ be the constant simplicial set on $\{0,1\}$, a Kan complex: every horn map is constant on each connected horn, and extends by that constant value. Define $a:M\to D$ to be constantly $0$, and define $b:M\to D$ to be $1$ on the component $[h]$ and $0$ elsewhere. These are simplicial maps because all vertices of a simplex are joined by its edges, and assigning its common component-label commutes with every face and degeneracy. The assumption gives $a q=b q$ in every degree. But $a$ and $b$ have different components in $\operatorname{Fun}(M,D)$: evaluation at a vertex in $[h]$ is a simplicial map $\operatorname{Fun}(M,D)\to D$, whose realization is continuous with discrete target $|D|=\{0,1\}$. It sends $a$ to $0$ and $b$ to $1$, so no path can join them. This contradicts the injectivity from step 3. These assertions use only the explicit simplicial definitions of spaces, products and internal functor sets in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].

source.place: Agent two-point test expanding the same-component step of Lemma 5.4.2.4, printed pp.424-425; it replaces use of the full total-space weak-equivalence theorem by its needed component consequence.

proof.text: Put $P_y=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(x,y)$, $A=\mathfrak C[\mathcal E]$, and let $p_y:|P_y|_Q\to P_y$ and $\theta_y:|P_y|_Q\to A(x,y)$ be the weak homotopy equivalences of [lem-coef-pinched-rigidification-resolution]. Let $u_y:A(x,y)\to\operatorname{Sing}|A(x,y)|$ be the weak homotopy equivalence of [lem-cbc-realization-singular-unit-weak]. By the definition of weak homotopy equivalence in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], each induces a component bijection. Thus $\beta_y=\pi_0(u_y)\pi_0(\theta_y)\pi_0(p_y)^{-1}$ is a bijection $\pi_0P_y\to\pi_0h_x(y)$, with this target identified by [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces]. The degree-zero formula in the pinched-resolution statement and the characteristic-map formula in the unit statement give $\beta_y([v])=[m_v]$ for every edge $v:x\to y$. This is composition of the cited component bijections and their stated vertex formulas; the compatibility with postcomposition is supplied separately in step 6.

source.place: Proposition 2.2.4.1 and Proposition 2.2.2.7, pinched rigidification comparison; compose the cited weak-equivalence statements on components. The realization/singular unit is the existing generic theorem lem-cbc-realization-singular-unit-weak (Kerodon Tag 0142).

proof.text: Let $i=p(e)$. The fiber and base-pullback clauses of [lem-coef-space-transport-classification] give $\xi\in\pi_0G(i)$ corresponding to $e\in E_i$, and step 2 gives $\pi_0(\lambda_i)(\xi)=[q(e)]=[m_h]$. By step 5 and the edge-representation clause of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition], choose $v:x\to F(i)$ with $\beta_{F(i)}([v])=\xi$. Fill the inner $2$-horn with edges $v,\iota_i$ using [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and write $w:x\to c$ for its long edge. Apply [lem-coef-rigidification-component-postcomposition] to this triangle and the very same $\beta$ of step 5. Since $\lambda_i=h_x(\iota_i)$, its triangle clause gives $\beta_c([w])=\pi_0(\lambda_i)(\xi)=[m_h]=\beta_c([h])$. Injectivity gives $[w]=[h]$, while the triangle clause of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] gives $[w]=[\iota_i][v]$. This proves the required equation with the original cocone leg. The comparison with enriched postcomposition is taken from the new cited theorem, not proved inline.

source.place: HTT Lemma 5.4.2.4, component/retract argument, printed pp.424-425. The separately stated rigidification-component-postcomposition lemma supplies the comparison previously hidden in returned step 5.

proof.text: If $c=x$ and $h=1_x$, the preceding factorization gives $v:x\to F(i)$ and the given $\iota_i:F(i)\to x$ with $[\iota_i v]=[1_x]$. By the homotopy-category and unit clauses of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition], the morphisms of $h\mathcal E$ are these connected components and its composition is the one just checked. Thus this is precisely $[\iota_i]\,[v]=1_x$. Hence $x$ is a retract of $F(i)$. Compactness entered only for the source $x$ in step 1, so no compactness of the stages is required.

source.place: Lemma 5.4.2.4, concluding retract argument, printed pp.424-425.

lean.statement: theorem compact_stage_factorization (γ : Cardinal.{u}) (_hγ : γ.IsRegular) (E : SSet.{max (u + 1) v}) [Quasicategory E] (_hE : Presentability.IsLocallySmall.{u, max (u + 1) v} E) (_hcolimits : Presentability.HasSmallKappaFilteredColimits E γ) (I : SSet.{max (u + 1) v}) [Quasicategory I] (_hsmall : Presentability.IsSmall.{u, max (u + 1) v} I) (_hfiltered : Presentability.IsKappaFiltered γ I) (F : I ⟶ E) (t : (coconeCategory F) _⦋0⦌) (_ht : IsColimiting F t) (x : E _⦋0⦌) (_hx : Presentability.IsKappaCompact E γ x) (h : (mappingSpace E x t.1.1) _⦋0⦌) : ∃ (i : I _⦋0⦌) (v : (mappingSpace E x (F.app _ i)) _⦋0⦌) (w : (mappingSpace E x t.1.1) _⦋0⦌) (s : E _⦋2⦌), E.δ 2 s = v.1 ∧ E.δ 0 s = (coconeHomotopy F t).app (op ⦋1⦌) (I.σ 0 i, stdSimplex.objEquiv.symm (𝟙 ⦋1⦌)) ∧ E.δ 1 s = w.1 ∧ π₀.mk w = π₀.mk h
lean.note: The general morphism clause and the identity/retract specialization use the original coherent cocone. A two-simplex specifies composition and equality in the right-pinched mapping space π₀ specifies homotopy. The added landed statement dependency supplies the existing coconeHomotopy extraction; no notion is duplicated.
